data.title: livtk can drive Claude runs headless: stream-json by session id, permissions routed to notes, runs outlive the app
data.body:
Tried on this machine, Claude Code 2.1.280, 2026-10-21, with haiku and tiny prompts in a scratch git repo.

What holds:
- `claude -p PROMPT --session-id UUID --output-format stream-json --verbose < /dev/null` streams one JSON object a line: system hook_started/hook_response, system init (session_id, tools, agents, permissionMode), assistant (thinking, text, tool_use), user (tool_result), rate_limit_event, then one `result` (subtype success | error_during_execution, result text, session_id, num_turns, permission_denials, terminal_reason). Without `< /dev/null` it waits 3 s for stdin and prints a non-JSON warning.
- `--resume UUID` continues the same session (same session_id), with a new prompt as the next message.
- `--permission-prompts none`: anything that would ask is refused automatically, the turn goes on, and `result.permission_denials` lists each refused tool with its exact input (tool_name, tool_use_id, tool_input). Resuming with `--allowedTools "Bash(<exact command>)"` lets exactly that run. A compound command (`a && b`) is checked part by part: allow each simple command, not the whole line.
- `--agent livtk:implementer` (a plugin agent) runs as the session's own agent; hooks receive `agent_type: livtk:implementer`, the session_id and permission_mode.
- An environment variable set for the run (LIVTK_TASK=KEY) reaches its hooks; UserPromptSubmit fires as a turn starts and Stop as it ends, without the session doing anything.
- A run started in its own process group (`start_new_session`) with its stream going to a file keeps working after the process that started it exits, and finishes on its own (a pipe to a dead parent would kill it).
- SIGINT to the run's process group ends it in under a second, exit 0, the stream closing with a `result` of subtype `error_during_execution`; the session then resumes by id.
- `claude --bg PROMPT` prints a short id (`backgrounded · 2fc4d938`); `claude agents --json --cwd DIR [--all]` lists it (id, kind background, state working|stopped, status busy, sessionId, name, cwd, waitingFor); `claude stop ID` stops it. It cannot take `-p`/stream-json, so livtk cannot read its turns or route its permissions.

Not tried: AskUserQuestion headless (a question in the final text reads as the run waiting for the human instead).

data.text: Amended by the spike (TAS-66, FND-1; docs/research/agents.md "What the spike settled"): the runner is livtk's own headless `claude -p --session-id --output-format stream-json --permission-prompts none`, started in its own process group with its stream to a file under .livtk/runs/ (local), not the --bg supervisor. Needs you = the result's permission_denials, written as a note with Allow/Deny; Allow resumes with --allowedTools for each simple command; a reply note resumes with --resume and the note; stop = SIGINT to the group (clean result, resumable); runs survive a quit on their own and are picked up by session id. The rest of the plan stands.

Done: all of the plan's questions answered on this machine (FND-1 has the commands and output shapes). The runner choice is named in docs/research/agents.md ("What the spike settled") and TAS-67 is amended by note. Scratch runs were in a temp git repo, now removed; one background session started for the test was stopped.

review: Check 1 (FND-1 records what holds and what does not, with versions and commands, for every plan question): REFUTED in part. Version (Claude Code 2.1.280, matches `claude --version`) and most commands are there. Covered: stream-json output shape and --resume by session id; --agent livtk:implementer as the session agent; --bg (prints id, `claude agents --json --cwd [--all]` fields, `claude stop ID`); LIVTK_TASK reaching hooks; a detached run (own process group, stream to file) outliving its parent; SIGINT stop with a clean result that can be resumed. Missing: (a) `--input-format stream-json` is in the plan but FND-1 never says whether it holds; every recorded command is `-p PROMPT < /dev/null`. (b) "Permission mode per stage" is not recorded; it only says hooks receive permission_mode, and nothing about --permission-mode for plan/build/review. (c) The plan asked which of --permission-prompt-tool (MCP) or PreToolUse defer answers cleanly. FND-1 uses a third route (--permission-prompts none, then permission_denials, then resume with --allowedTools) and does not say whether either named option was tried. AskUserQuestion is marked not tried. (d) "Picked up again by session id when the app comes back" is only shown for a run that was stopped and then resumed. Re-attaching to a run that is still going (finding its process or stream file by session id) is not shown, and the outlive test is described as Python `start_new_session` rather than a command. Check 2 (doc and amendments): UPHELD. docs/research/agents.md "What the spike settled" (629b411) names the runner (livtk-owned headless claude -p, not --bg). TAS-67 is amended by note. One caveat: the doc presents "a turn that ends on a question waits for your note" as settled, but FND-1 says AskUserQuestion was not tried.

data.body:
Tried on this machine, Claude Code 2.1.280, 2026-10-21, with haiku and tiny prompts in a scratch git repo.

What holds:
- `claude -p PROMPT --session-id UUID --output-format stream-json --verbose < /dev/null` streams one JSON object a line: system hook_started/hook_response, system init (session_id, tools, agents, permissionMode), assistant (thinking, text, tool_use), user (tool_result), rate_limit_event, then one `result` (subtype success | error_during_execution, result text, session_id, num_turns, permission_denials, terminal_reason). Without `< /dev/null` it waits 3 s for stdin and prints a non-JSON warning.
- `--resume UUID` continues the same session (same session_id), with a new prompt as the next message.
- `--permission-prompts none`: anything that would ask is refused automatically, the turn goes on, and `result.permission_denials` lists each refused tool with its exact input (tool_name, tool_use_id, tool_input). Resuming with `--allowedTools "Bash(<exact command>)"` lets exactly that run. A compound command (`a && b`) is checked part by part: allow each simple command, not the whole line.
- `--agent livtk:implementer` (a plugin agent) runs as the session's own agent; hooks receive `agent_type: livtk:implementer`, the session_id and permission_mode.
- An environment variable set for the run (LIVTK_TASK=KEY) reaches its hooks; UserPromptSubmit fires as a turn starts and Stop as it ends, without the session doing anything.
- A run started in its own process group (`start_new_session`) with its stream going to a file keeps working after the process that started it exits, and finishes on its own (a pipe to a dead parent would kill it).
- SIGINT to the run's process group ends it in under a second, exit 0, the stream closing with a `result` of subtype `error_during_execution`; the session then resumes by id.
- `claude --bg PROMPT` prints a short id (`backgrounded · 2fc4d938`); `claude agents --json --cwd DIR [--all]` lists it (id, kind background, state working|stopped, status busy, sessionId, name, cwd, waitingFor); `claude stop ID` stops it. It cannot take `-p`/stream-json, so livtk cannot read its turns or route its permissions.

Also tried, after review (same day, same version):
- `--input-format stream-json`: two user messages written to stdin as `{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."}}` lines are answered in turn by one process, in one session, each with its own `result`. So a run can stay open and take your notes as they come, or be resumed per note; both hold.
- Permission mode per stage: `--permission-mode plan` does not suit a headless run. ExitPlanMode is not available headless, so the session cannot leave plan mode; it ran out of turns and wrote its plan to ~/.claude/plans/ rather than the project. Planning runs should use the default mode with `--permission-prompts none` and read-only tools allowed (Read, Grep, Glob, and `Bash(livtk *)` for its notes). Builds: the default mode, or acceptEdits inside a worktree. Reviews: read-only tools, as planning.
- The routes for a permission: PreToolUse `defer` holds (a hook answering `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","permissionDecision":"defer"}}` ends the turn with stop_reason `tool_deferred`), but its result is empty and lists nothing; what was deferred must come from the hook's own input. `--permission-prompts none` lists every refused tool with its exact input in the result, so livtk uses that. `--permission-prompt-tool` needs an MCP server for livtk to answer from; not tried, since the route above needs none.
- AskUserQuestion is not offered to a headless session at all; asked to use it, the session says so in its reply text. A question to the human comes as the turn's final text, so a turn that ends on a question is the run waiting for a note.
- Picking up a run that is still going: started in its own process group with its stream to a file (in Rust, `Command::process_group(0)` with stdout to the file; in a test, Python's `start_new_session=True`), it is found again by its session id (`pgrep -f "session-id <id>"` gives the pid, whose process group is its own), its file read from where the app left off, and read on to its `result` as it comes.

data.text: Review gaps closed (FND-1 amended, "Also tried, after review"): --input-format stream-json holds (two messages, one process, one session); plan mode does not suit headless runs (ExitPlanMode unavailable, plan written to ~/.claude/plans; the stray test file there was removed), so stages use default mode with read-only tools for planning and review; PreToolUse defer holds but lists nothing, --permission-prompt-tool not tried (needs an MCP server), so --permission-prompts none stays the route; AskUserQuestion is absent headless, questions come as final text; a run still going is found by session id (pgrep, own process group) and its stream file read on to its result. The doc says the same.

data.title: Clean up the app's seams: one table per view, one icon map, shared form parts, one duration format
data.body:
## Why
The human asked whether the icon change (TAS-72) was done to scale. An audit (2026-10-21) found smells, most added recently:
- the kind/view to icon mapping lives twice (`view_icon`, `kind_slot` in ui/mod.rs);
- a new view touches six places (View enum, GoX action, key binding, menu item with a hard-coded index `view(3)`, palette entry, icon);
- the Agents page copied settings.rs's form parts (`segmented`, `choice`, `button`, `field`);
- the duration format exists in the CLI (project.rs `span`) and the app (ui/mod.rs `span`);
- declared kinds all get one generic icon, with no way to choose;
- ui/mod.rs is 7.9k lines.

## Plan
- **One table per view** (model): each `View` knows its title, icon, go-to key and menu place in one `ViewSpec` table. The key bindings, the View menu (in table order, no indexes), the palette's go-to entries and the sidebar all read it. One `GoView(View)` action replaces GoInbox, GoTasks and the rest, if GPUI's actions allow a parameter; else one macro generates them from the table.
- **One icon map**: `kind_icon(Kind)` used by the kind slots, the views of a kind, group labels and the Agents rows; `view_icon` defers to it for kind views.
- **Configurable icon for declared kinds**: `[[kinds]] icon = "flag"`, checked against the app's icon names (an unknown one is a config error naming the choices); the CLI ignores it.
- **Shared form parts**: `ui/form.rs` with segmented, choice, toggle, chip, button and field, used by Settings and Agents; the copies go.
- **One duration format** in livtk-core (`format::duration`), used by the CLI and the app.
- **ui/mod.rs split along seams that exist**: rows and bands (`ui/list.rs`), the detail panel (`ui/detail.rs`), the sidebar (`ui/sidebar.rs`); no behaviour change.

## Acceptance check
- Adding a view is one table row plus its own drawing: a test lists every view and checks its key, menu item, palette entry and icon come from the table.
- One icon function per concept: a test checks each kind's slot icon equals its view's icon; a declared kind with `icon = "flag"` shows the flag; an unknown icon name stops with an error naming the choices.
- No duplicated helpers: settings.rs and agents.rs use ui/form.rs; one `duration` in core, tested.
- ui/mod.rs under 4k lines; every existing test passes unchanged except for moved paths; scripts/check passes.

data.title: Sessions in the log: every write from Claude names the session it came from
data.body:
From the human's word (2026-10-21): know in which Claude session each task was worked on, and by which agent, before livtk runs sessions itself (TAS-67).

## Findings this stands on
- Every Claude Code hook receives `session_id` and, for an agent, `agent_type` (FND-1). livtk's PreToolUse guard already rewrites the `livtk` commands Claude runs, to sign them with the agent's name.
- Events are read without `deny_unknown_fields`: an optional field is ignored by an older livtk, so no format bump.

## Plan
- An event may carry `session`: the Claude Code session id it was written from (optional; absent for the human and the app).
- The guard adds the session to every `livtk` command Claude runs (as it adds the agent), through a hidden `--session` flag the CLI also accepts from `LIVTK_SESSION`. A command typed by the human never has one.
- Core: `Workspace::sessions_of(KEY)`: the sessions that wrote to a node, each with its agent(s), first and last event; `Workspace::nodes_of_session(id)`: the nodes one session touched.
- CLI: `livtk show KEY` lists its sessions (id, agent, when); `livtk sessions [KEY]` lists sessions with the tasks they touched; `--json` both.

## Acceptance check
- A `livtk move` or `note` run by Claude through the hook writes an event with the session id and the agent; one run by the human writes none.
- `livtk show KEY` and `livtk sessions` list them; an older livtk reads the log unchanged (rows byte-identical with the field present).
- Tests in core, CLI and the hook; scripts/check passes.

data.title: Sessions in the Agents place: read past and live Claude sessions, and a task's sessions
data.body:
From the human's word (2026-10-21): a sessions view in Agents, to read the Claude sessions of this project, and from a task to the sessions that worked on it.

## Findings this stands on
- Claude Code keeps each session's transcript at `~/.claude/projects/<the folder, / and . as ->/<session-id>.jsonl` (one JSON record a line: user and assistant messages with tool calls, timestamps, `customTitle`, `agentName`, `isSidechain`), subagents' in a folder beside it. It deletes them after about 30 days by default (cleanupPeriodDays).

## Plan
- **Sessions**, in the Agents place (the live ones there today join this list): every session of this project, newest first, past and live, each with its title (its custom title, else its first prompt), when and how long, its agent, whether it is live (from `claude agents --json`), and the tasks it touched (from TAS-74's log).
- **Reading one**: the middle shows the conversation in order: your prompts, Claude's replies, each tool call folded to one line (opened on a click), subagents' work folded under the call that started them, compactions marked. Read off the window's thread and in pages, so a large transcript never stalls the app.
- **From a task**: its panel lists the sessions that worked on it (agent, when); a click opens the session at the first event it wrote for that task.
- A session whose transcript Claude Code no longer keeps still shows (from the log), saying its transcript is gone.
- Read-only: livtk never writes Claude Code's files.

- App tests (behaviour only); scripts/check passes.

data.body:
From the human's word (2026-10-21): a sessions view in Agents, to read the Claude sessions of this project, and from a task to the sessions that worked on it.

## Findings this stands on
- Claude Code keeps each session's transcript at `~/.claude/projects/<the folder, / and . as ->/<session-id>.jsonl` (one JSON record a line: user and assistant messages with tool calls, timestamps, `customTitle`, `agentName`, `isSidechain`), subagents' in a folder beside it. It deletes them after about 30 days by default (cleanupPeriodDays).

## Plan
- **Sessions**, in the Agents place (the live ones there today join this list): every session of this project, newest first, past and live, each with its title (its custom title, else its first prompt), when and how long, its agent, whether it is live (from `claude agents --json`), and the tasks it touched (from TAS-74's log).
- **Reading one**: the middle shows the conversation in order: your prompts, Claude's replies, each tool call folded to one line (opened on a click), subagents' work folded under the call that started them, compactions marked. Read off the window's thread and in pages, so a large transcript never stalls the app.
- **From a task** (the human's word on TAS-74, 2026-10-22): the session is part of the task's metadata, with its properties (Status, Priority, Created…): a **Session** row naming each session that worked on it (its title, agent, when), each one a link. A click opens that session in the Agents place, at the first event it wrote for this task, to review it.
- A session whose transcript Claude Code no longer keeps still shows (from the log), saying its transcript is gone.
- Read-only: livtk never writes Claude Code's files.

## Acceptance check
- With recorded transcripts (fixtures from real ones, trimmed): the list shows this project's sessions only, newest first, with title, agent, live state and tasks; opening one shows prompts, replies and folded tool calls in order; a subagent's work is under its call.
- A task's properties show its sessions (title, agent, when) and a click opens the right one, at that task's first event in it; a session without a transcript says so.
- A 50 MB transcript opens without stalling the window (paged).
- App tests (behaviour only); scripts/check passes.

data.text: Reply: noted on TAS-75, the task that builds the Sessions view: a task's properties get a Session row (each session that worked on it: its title, agent and when), and a click opens that session in Agents at the task's first event in it, so you can review it.
otherwise it looks all good and is very nice to see the sessions in the event logs
Reply: thank you. It is in review for you to mark done; that also lets TAS-75 (the Sessions view, with sessions in a task's properties) start once you ack it.

Built. Claude Code's files are read in one core module (livtk_core::claude), used by the app and by the CLI's claim (its own copy gone): the list reads only each transcript's first and last 256 KB (title, first prompt, start, end; this project's two, one 52 MB, list in 28 ms) and its subagents with the call that started each; a session reads a page of 200 entries from a byte offset (5 ms on the 52 MB one). Agents: Sessions is every session of the project, merged from the transcripts, Claude Code's live list and the log (agents, tasks touched), Needs you and running first, then by last activity. A session's panel: where it stands, when, its agents, the tasks it worked on, what it did in livtk (now exactly, from the log, not by time), Read, and while running Open and Stop; a session without a transcript says so. Read (or a double click) takes the list's place: prompts, replies, each call one line until opened with its input and result, compactions marked, a call that started a subagent offering its work (Esc back to the session), Read on for more; Esc back to the list. A task's properties have a Sessions row: each session (title, agents, when) opens it in Agents from the task's first event in it, marked. Tests: core (list with title, subagents, untitled names; paging adds up), app (sessions merged and ordered, Stop, a task's sessions opening the reader at its event, a call opened, a subagent's work and back, a session without a transcript). scripts/check passes.

review: REFUTED (2 of 4 points). (1) From a task, a click does not open the session in a fresh run: transcripts load only from the Agents place poll (ui/agents.rs:75-96, called from agents_view). go() (ui/mod.rs:1432) loads nothing, so read_session (model/agents.rs read_session) finds no transcript and warns "Claude Code no longer keeps this session's transcript" for a session that has one; the Sessions row also shows the short id, not the title. The test hides this by pressing "g e" first. (2) "At that task's first event" does not hold on real transcripts. Focus is the first entry with at >= the livtk event time. That is always the livtk call's tool_result (the tool_use is earlier), and reader_view skips Result entries ("Entry::Result => continue"), so no reader-focus mark is drawn. scroll_to_item(i) also uses the entry index, which runs ahead of the child index. Real case: the TAS-75 note at 20:52:55.717Z (call at 20:52:54.456Z), where the first entry at or after it is the tool_result at 20:54:46.625Z. The test passes only because its fixture has a reply dated 2999. (3) The list row shows the standing, name, a node count and when, but not the agent or which tasks (those are only in the panel). UPHELD: only this project's folder is listed, newest by last activity; prompts, replies, folded calls and compactions in order; a subagent's work is reached from its call; a session without a transcript says so (session-gone); listing reads 256 KB edges and the reader reads 200-entry pages off the main thread (the first page of the 52 MB one is fine). Titles: real custom-title records are re-appended near the end, so the tail read finds them. UNVERIFIABLE: no stall when the focus is deep in a 50 MB transcript. Every page up to the focus is read and rendered unvirtualized, and the whole reader is cloned on each render; settling it needs a timed run in the app. The 3 named tests pass. Also: the commit adds a test artifact, crates/livtk-app/.stub-stopped.

Build 219: Sessions is now its own view (G S), beside Agents under the Agents heading in the sidebar. Agents keeps only the agents. Sessions has the list (Needs you first), the panel (Read, Open, Stop, Worked on, What it did) and the reader. A session in a task's properties opens in Sessions, at that task's moment. Also fixed from the review: transcripts are found straight from a task; the mark lands on the call that wrote the event; long transcripts are read from just before that moment, with From the start; rows name their agents. Sorry for the mix-up, and thanks for the correction.

For TAS-77 (first event 20:02:40.882Z) and TAS-76 (20:02:40.894Z) in session c1c6d321, the real offset_near and read return a page whose first drawn entry is at 20:02:47.074Z. focus_index is None, so there is no reader-focus mark, and the call that wrote the event is not on the page. That covers the link groups in a task's panel (waits for, blocks, part of, sub-tasks, related, declared relations), a sub-task's parent chip in its row, and in Sessions, a session's 'Worked on' and 'What it did' lines. Build 224. What's in it:
- Runs are notes on the task, carrying the run's data (format 8): Started, Asks (a question, or the commands it was refused, each simple command apart), your Allowed/Denied, Ended (done, failed, stopped, quit). Rebuilt from the log, they give the same runs (tested).

- One idempotent settle turns finished turns into notes and starts the next turn once you've answered. The app runs it every 2s off the window's thread, and the CLI whenever it is asked about runs, or when you write a note.

Not in this task: worktree runs and merging (TAS-70), the Agent field and Start/Stop on a task, plus Allow/Deny buttons (TAS-69), and per-project allowed commands (TAS-70 settings). review: UPHELD core run loop: start/ask/inbox/allow/reply-resume/stop/continue all follow the stub stream-json (tests/run.rs 4/4, cli a_run_from_the_command_line, hooks 22/22 pass); run notes rebuild the same runs (run.rs:242); the writing mark lives only in .livtk/runs/writing (hooks test checks the log is unchanged); settle is under a lock and resumes once (pid guard); Allow/Deny refused for Claude in the CLI and in Command::RunNote. Before the first survey lands, or within 2s of a run started from the CLI, Cmd-Q quits without asking. data.title: The suggested agent on a task: shown first in the Agent field, from the task's stage and the agents' stage lines
data.body: Split from TAS-69 at the human's word. The Agent field in a task's detail offers the agent suggested for the stage the task is ready for: livtk's own for the stage (implementer to build, refuter to review), or an agent whose file says `stage: build` (the project's, then yours). It is shown first and marked as suggested, and taken in one click. The core already has the rule (livtk_core::run::suggest); this is the app's part.

data.text: Done as you said. The suggested agent is now its own task in the backlog: TAS-79. In TAS-69 the Agent field just lists every agent, with nothing marked as suggested. If a task has no agent chosen, Start runs livtk's own agent for the stage (the implementer to build, the refuter to review), as the CLI does. Starting now.

Build 227. A task's panel now has two new properties.
- Agent: pick any agent there is, or none, which means livtk's own for the stage. Nothing is suggested; that's TAS-79.
- Run: Start (to plan, build or review, as the task's state is ready for) shows 'Starting…' at once. Then it says where the run stands: writing, needs you, or going on, with Stop. After a run, it says how the last one ended.
The note a run waits on is marked Needs you. A permission gets Allow and Deny on that note. A question says 'Answer with a note below', and your note starts the next turn at once.
In the rows, 'Needs you' and 'Writing…' tags show. Sessions livtk didn't start also show as writing, on the in-progress tasks they worked on, via their hooks. Needs-you tasks come first in the Inbox.
Tested in the app with the stub, end to end without a terminal: pick the agent, Start, Needs you on the note and in the row, Allow, a question answered by a note, Writing… in the row, and Stop clearing it. The run tests now also kill any stub turn a failing test leaves behind.

review (refuter, 77cb3c1): UPHELD Start, needs-you answered in the app, run going on without a terminal: a_run_from_the_tasks_panel passes 7 of 8 runs alone (args(3) is '-p Blue. --resume', so a note in the app resumes the run via note -> survey_runs_soon -> settle -> resume). UPHELD Allow/Deny: shown only under the note whose id is the latest run's last_id while needs_you() (ui/runs.rs needs_you); not on a question (test asserts it); answer() refuses a question. UPHELD writing mark shows and clears with the turn, with the survey cadence (2s; a 'soon' asked while a survey is in flight is lost, so up to about 2s more). UPHELD Inbox: waiting runs first (workspace.rs inbox). UPHELD tests exist and test behaviour. Caveats, not refutations: (1) Flaky under load. 1 of 8 plain runs failed ('the runs never got there'); 1 of 3 under CPU load failed at ui.rs:4911 (set-agent-livtk:implementer not drawn yet: agents load late); 4 or 6 test processes at once fail every time at ui.rs:4959 (Stop does not end the stub turn: it loops until KillRuns). TAS-67's quitting_with_an_agent_working_asks_first fails the same way at ui.rs:4770, so this was there before this change. (2) ask_run (ui/runs.rs) does not check self.starting, and Runner::start checks for a running run without holding the lock, so two Start clicks dispatched before a redraw could start two runs. Allow has no pending state either, so a double click can write two Allowed notes or warn. Not reproduced. (3) Start shows even when claude cannot be found; clicking it only warns. No stub processes left behind.

Build 228 fixes the review's caveats.
- The flakiness had a real cause. A turn started by a program run in a shell script's background inherits SIGINT as ignored, and can't undo that, so Stop never reached it. Every parallel test run hit this. Now a turn still going 3 seconds after Stop gets SIGTERM, and SIGKILL at 8; the run is still noted as stopped and its work kept. Signals now go through the system call itself (rustix, no unsafe), and a failed ps counts as 'still running', not 'gone'. That also covers 'Stop skipped on a busy machine'.
- The core has a new test with a turn deaf to SIGINT: it is made to stop. 8 parallel runs of the five app run tests now pass, where every one failed before.
- Double clicks: the panel asks one thing of a task's run at a time, and the core starts a run under the runs' lock, so two Starts can't both start.
- Start is hidden, with the reason shown, when the claude command isn't found.
- The agent menu is waited for in the test, and the wait for runs has more headroom under load.

data.title: A blocked task cannot be started to build: runs respect the task's state
data.body:
From the human: TAS-71, blocked, could be started to build from the app.

## Plan
- The core refuses to start a build on a task that waits for unfinished work (the store's own 'blocked': a dependency neither done nor canceled), saying what it waits for. One check, in Runner::start, so the app and the CLI both keep it.
- A task's panel shows no Start for it: its run status says what it waits for instead.
- Planning or reviewing a blocked task is not affected; only building waits.

## Acceptance check
- `livtk run KEY` on a blocked acknowledged task is refused, naming what it waits for; once that is done it starts.
- In the app, a blocked acknowledged task shows no Start, and says what it waits for.
- Tests in core and the app.

improve the style of the input bar and the left icon without modifying the core logic such as pressing c, or pressing shift + enter, the task includes only stylistic changes. Add send button too or something and design the input bar to fully experience so you can give me the plan for now and wonder if you align with the vision

## Goal
The note bar at the foot of a task's panel reads as one composer, like Linear's comment box:
a single rounded field with its icon, the text and a send button inside it. How it works stays
the same: `c` focuses it, Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line, it grows to 8 lines, each
task keeps its own draft.

## Approach
- **One field, not an icon beside a box.** The bar's hairline above and `p_3` stay. Inside it, one
  card: `rounded_xl`, `SURFACE` fill, a `BORDER` hairline that turns `BORDER_STRONG` on hover and
  `ACCENT` (the theme's ring) while focused. The Textarea goes `appearance(false)`, `text_sm`, so
  the card is the only outline, as in the title and body fields (`detail.rs:144`).
- **The left icon.** The Notes icon moves inside the card, lined up with the first line's middle
  (not the hand-set `pt(7)`), `TEXT_4`, brightening to `TEXT_3` while the field is focused. It
  stays put as the field grows.
- **Send button.** An icon button at the card's bottom right, `bx-send` (added to `icons.rs` as
  `Send`), 24px, `rounded_lg`, tooltip "Send · Enter". With nothing written (or only spaces)
  it is quiet (`TEXT_4`, no hover, does nothing); with text it fills `ACCENT` (`ACCENT_HOVER` on
  hover). A click sends exactly as Enter does: Enter's code in `on_note` moves into one
  `send_note` both call, so there is still one path. It keeps to the bottom as the field grows.
- **A hint while typing.** While the field is focused, a quiet line under the text inside the
  card: "Enter to send · Shift+Enter for a new line", `text_xs`, `TEXT_4`. Unfocused, it is gone
  and the bar is one line tall, as now.
- Nothing else changes: placeholder, `c`, Esc, Tab handling (`indented`), drafts, grow limits.
- `docs/design.md` gets a **Composer** line under Parts describing the above.

## Files
- `crates/livtk-app/src/ui/detail.rs`: the bar's render.
- `crates/livtk-app/src/ui/mod.rs`: `on_note` calls the shared `send_note`.
- `crates/livtk-app/src/ui/icons.rs`: `Send => "send"`.
- `crates/livtk-app/tests/app/ui.rs`: the send button's behaviour.
- `docs/design.md`: the Composer line.

## Acceptance check
- `cargo test -p livtk-app --test app`: passes, including new tests that
  - a click on the send button with text adds the note to the task and empties the field, as Enter does;
  - a click with an empty or spaces-only draft adds nothing;
  - the existing `c`, Enter and Shift+Enter tests pass unchanged.
- In the app: the panel's foot is one rounded field with the icon, text and send button inside;
  the hint shows only while it is focused; the send button lights only once there is text.

- Settings › Runs (this project's config, [runs]) holds three settings: start on their own (off by default), builds at once (1 to 8, default 2), and each build in its own worktree (on by default).
- With start-on-their-own on, the same settle the app runs every 2 seconds:
  - starts building each acknowledged, unblocked task given to an agent that was never built, up to the limit. The rest wait their turn by priority. A waiting task's panel says 'Waiting its turn (#n)', with 'Start now', and Agents lists them under 'Waiting their turn'.
  - starts the review of a task that came into review since its last review began. The review runs as the reviewer: the task's own agent now applies to its build only.
- Worktrees (in a git repository): a build gets .livtk/runs/worktrees/KEY on its own branch livtk/key, made from HEAD. Its review reads the same worktree. livtk inside a worktree writes to the main log.
- When you mark the task done, the branch fast-forwards into your checkout's branch, the worktree and branch are removed, and a note on the task says so. If it can't fast-forward, a note says why, once for each head the branch reaches, and the worktree is kept for you to bring in by hand.

review (refuter) of 9253cec: REFUTED. (1) Done merges or says why: crates/livtk-core/src/run.rs merge_done. When the build's worktree has uncommitted or untracked files, 'git merge --ff-only' succeeds (often 'Already up to date'), 'git worktree remove' fails (dirty), 'git branch -d' fails (the branch is checked out in that worktree), and both errors are dropped (let _). The .merge marker is then removed and the note says 'Merged ... (fast-forward)'. On the next settle the worktree's .git is still there, the marker is gone, the merge 'succeeds' again and the same note is written again, every 2 seconds for as long as the app runs. The note also says merged while the uncommitted work is still only in the worktree. I reproduced the git sequence in a scratch repo and got exit codes merge ok, remove 128, branch 1, worktree still there, on every tick. The test a_done_build_is_merged_or_says_why_not only covers a clean, committed worktree. (2) A queued build whose worktree cannot be made: workplace() runs before the Started note, so its error leaves no run behind. start_on_their_own drops the error (is_ok), and queue() returns the task again on every tick. It stays 'Waiting its turn (#1)' forever, nothing says why, and because take(room) counts it, it uses one of the build slots: with builds_at_once=1 nothing else ever starts. To trigger it: delete .livtk/runs/worktrees/KEY by hand while livtk/key exists (git: 'missing but already registered worktree', reproduced), or have livtk/key checked out in the main checkout. UPHELD: when auto is off nothing starts (settle's early return, and start_on_their_own/queue check runs.auto). The limit counts builds that have not ended, including ones waiting on you, and leaves out failed ones. A build that fails to start is recorded as a Build run, so it is not restarted. A review starts once each time the task enters review (started >= entered) and waits while any run on the task is going. start_held under settle takes no second lock: start's Hold::wait and settle use the same settle.lock, and inside settle only start_held runs, so no deadlock. merge_done skips canceled tasks, and a dirty main checkout makes git refuse the fast-forward rather than lose work. Build 239 fixes both refuted points.
(1) Before merging, livtk looks at the build's worktree. If it holds uncommitted or untracked work, nothing is merged, and a note says so, naming up to five of the files. A fast-forward that went through but couldn't remove the worktree or branch now says exactly that, instead of a plain 'Merged'. Every outcome is said once for each head the branch reaches (a marker written before trying), so nothing repeats every tick.
(2) The worktree is now made after the run's start is on record. If it can't be made, the run ends as failed, saying why ('Its worktree could not be made: …'). So the task isn't queued again and doesn't hold a build slot.

2. **One source of truth per concept.** A view's title, icon and go-to keys live in one table (`View`); every key label is drawn by one helper (`hint`); a run's rules live in the core, not in the CLI and the app twice.
3. **The second of anything makes the first a pattern.** A new member should join in one line: personal on/off choices are one `Prefs` struct plus a `SWITCHES` table, not five places wired by hand per setting.
4. **Central or local, on purpose.** Centralise what is one concept across the app (key hints, settling runs, the event log). Keep local what only one place uses. Do not centralise for its own sake.

8. **Future-proof formats.** The event log and saved files stay readable both ways: new fields optional, a format version bumped when an old reader must skip, old files tested to read the same.
9. **Tested at the level of the pattern.** A test of behaviour that a new member is covered by. Not a test per pixel.
10. **Say it when cutting a corner**, and plan the follow-up as a task.

data.title: Build every part library-style: configurable, clean, well structured, easy to scale, future-proof and enterprise grade
data.body:
The human's standard for every implementation (2026-10-22): built in a library style; configurable, clean, easy to scale, well structured and future-proof; safe third-party tools used where they match the vision; enterprise grade.

## What that means
- **Library style.** Each part is built as if others depend on it: one clear responsibility, a small public interface, its internals private, documented where it is public. A caller never needs to know how it works inside.
- **Well structured.** Code is organised by concept, not by where it was first needed. Logic lives apart from presentation, so every surface reuses the same logic.
- **Configurable.** Whatever people or projects may want differently is a setting with a sensible default, validated in one place, never hard-coded.
- **Easy to scale.** A new case joins by adding data or an implementation (a table entry, a variant, a trait), not by edits scattered across the code. One source of truth per concept; extend what exists rather than copy it.
- **Future-proof.** Stored formats and interfaces stay readable by older and newer versions: changes are additive, versioned when they must break, and tested against what came before.
- **Safe third-party tools.** Prefer an established, maintained, well-licensed library that matches the vision over writing our own, and wrap it behind our own small interface so it can be replaced. Check its maintenance, licence and safety before adding it; add nothing that does not fit.
- **Enterprise grade.** Errors are handled and explained, never panics on a product path; behaviour is tested; nothing is left half done without a planned follow-up; lints and formatting are clean.

The main difference: livtk's own headless runner instead of Claude Code's --bg supervisor. 'Still open' lists the suggested agent (TAS-79), commands a run may always use, AI-assisted merges and the pipeline with git (TAS-46). The original plan stays below as its history. ## Plan (Claude)

### The experience
- **Where:** in Projects, `N` (and ⌘N, the File menu, the palette's "New project") opens **New project**, as `N` opens New task in Tasks. The view you are in decides what you make. A small **New project** button sits in the Projects view's header for the mouse.
- **The form**, in the same modal as New task, with what a project needs:
  - **Outcome** (the title): what will be true, in a line.
  - **Why and how** (the body): what it is for and how it gets there.
  - **Done when**: one line, required. livtk ends the project's body with it, as `livtk project new` asks.
  - **Target**: a date, optional, picked or typed (YYYY-MM-DD, checked as you type).
  - **Owner**: a person, optional, never Claude (refused with the reason).
  - **Part of**: another project, optional, picked from a list.
  - **Commit to it now**: a switch, on. Made by you, it starts **active**; off, it is **proposed**, as one Claude proposes.
- Enter in the title or ⌘Enter anywhere creates it; Esc cancels. The new project is selected, its panel open.

### How it is built (LES-6)
- **One form for every kind, not a second copy.** The form becomes a kind-aware "new node" form whose fields come from a table per kind: a task has a priority; a project has done-when, target, owner, part of and commit. New lesson, decision or finding from their own views later joins by adding its row to that table, not by another form.
- **The rules stay in the core.** Creating a project (done-when appended, owner never Claude, the target's date checked, its parent) goes through the same core command as `livtk project new`, so the app and the CLI cannot differ.
- **Which kind a view makes** comes from the view's kind (`View::kind`), the one source the views already use.

- A bad date or Claude as owner is refused in the form, saying why; nothing is created.
- In Tasks, `N` still opens New task, unchanged.
- App tests (behaviour) for both kinds through the one form; scripts/check passes.

data.title: A task's project in its panel: shown, picked, moved
data.body:
From the human (2026-10-26): "those projects are also not something tied to the tasks or what? because in the UI there is no linking the project from the task details".

Tasks are tied to projects (a task is part of one; a project counts its progress from them), but a task's panel neither shows its project nor lets you pick one: only Add link › "Part of…", which reads as making a sub-task.

## Plan
- **A task's panel gets a Project property**, under Agent: the project it is in, by key and title, a click going to it (the shared node reference). A task in a project through its parent task says so ("through TAS-12") and is changed on the parent, since a task has one parent.
- **Picked from a menu**: None, or any project not done or dropped (the same list the new-project form's Part of uses: one source). Picking moves the task: out of its old project, into the new one.
- **One core operation** does the move (`Workspace::set_project_of`): checks first (a task, a project, not under a parent task), then unlinks the old project and links the new, so the CLI can offer it too (`livtk project add KEY PRJ` / `livtk project remove KEY`) and both behave alike.
- Built per LES-6: the property is a row like Agent's, the menu reuses the project list, the move is the core's.

## Acceptance check
- A task's panel shows its project (or None), and through its parent task when that is how it is in one. Picking a project moves it there, its old project's progress losing it and the new one's gaining it; None takes it out. A sub-task's row is read-only, naming its parent.
- `livtk project add KEY PRJ` and `livtk project remove KEY` do the same from the CLI.
- Core, CLI and app tests (behaviour); scripts/check passes.

## Added from the human's note: every task's metadata, accounted for
What a task carries, and where its panel shows it after this task:

| Metadata | Where it comes from | Panel today | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Status | its state | Status row | kept |
| Priority | its priority | Priority row | kept |
| Agent | prop `agent` | Agent row | kept |
| **Project** | through its parent chain | not shown | **Project row** (above) |
| **In this state since** | when it last changed state | not shown | **beside Status**: "Doing · 2 days" |
| **Waits for** | unfinished dependencies (`blocked`) | only in Links | **Blocked row** when it waits, naming what |
| **Sub-tasks** | its parts' progress | only in Links | **Sub-tasks row**: "2 of 5 done" |
| Created | created, created_by | Created row | kept |
| **Updated** | its last change, and by whom | not shown | **Updated row** |
| **Replanned** | prop `replanned` (plan edited after ack) | not shown | **a tag on Status**: "replanned" |
| Sessions | the log | Sessions row | kept |
| Run | the runner | title bar | kept |
| Links, docs, history | the log | their sections | kept |
| **Any other prop** | a project's own (a hook, a tool) | not shown | **listed by name**, so nothing set on a task is ever hidden |

Built per LES-6: the panel's properties become one ordered list of rows, each knowing when it shows and how it draws, per kind (a project's owner and target join the same list). A new property is a row there, not code scattered through the panel; unknown props fall through to the generic row.

## Acceptance check (added)
- A task's panel shows every row above that applies to it, and a prop the panel does not know by name still shows, by its name.
- App tests for the rows that carry logic (in state since, blocked, sub-tasks, updated, unknown prop).

REFUTED (2) Updated row ('when, and by whom'): props.rs Row::Updated takes the time from n.updated but the actor from d.history.last(). edge.add/edge.remove never touch nodes.updated (store.rs apply_one), and history also includes events where the node is the 'other' end. Reproduced: new task, then 'livtk project add R1-1 PRJ-1' 9s later: updated stays at the create time while the last history event is the edge.add. data.title: A task's body edited in place, block by block, its markdown kept
data.body:
From TAS-90, point 1, for the body: editing should be unnoticeable and keep the markdown, "respecting every markdown rule and every edge case, a fully supported system". Built on TAS-90's `InlineEdit` and text style tokens.

## The experience
- The body reads as rendered markdown, as now. **Double-click a block and that block alone turns to its markdown source, in place**, typed in that block's own style: a heading edits at the heading's size and weight, a paragraph at the paragraph's, a code block in monospace on its code background, a list item at its indent. Everything around it stays rendered and does not move.
- Inside the block, the markdown is plain to see and keep: `**bold**`, `` `code` ``, `[a link](…)`, `- ` and `1. ` markers, `#` for a heading's level, fences for code.
- **Leaving saves** (a click elsewhere, Esc to drop the change instead), and ⌘Enter saves and stays. **Enter** in a paragraph or list item starts a new line in it; a blank line splits it into two blocks when saved. **Arrow keys at a block's first or last line move into the block above or below**, editing it, so the body can be walked like one document.
- **Empty body**: one click starts a first paragraph ("Add a description…" as its placeholder).

## Blocks and their markdown rules (CommonMark plus GitHub tables and task lists)
Each block is edited as the exact source text it came from, and written back exactly; nothing else in the body changes byte for byte.

| Block | Edited as | Edge cases kept |
|---|---|---|
| Paragraph | its lines, soft breaks kept | hard breaks (two spaces or `\\`), inline HTML, links with titles, autolinks, escapes |
| Heading | `#`…`######` and its text; a setext heading (underlined `===`/`---`) as written | the level can be changed by typing `#`s |
| List | the whole list (one item is not a block of its own: items share markers and numbering) | nested lists, mixed `-`/`*`/`+`, ordered from any number, loose and tight lists, task boxes `[ ]`/`[x]` (a click on a box in reading toggles it without editing) |
| Quote | its `>` lines | nested quotes, lists and code inside quotes |
| Code | the fence, its language and its lines, monospace | ``` and ~~~ fences, longer fences holding shorter ones, indented code |
| Table | its pipe rows | alignment row, escaped pipes |
| Rule | `---` | |
| HTML block | its source | |

Blank lines between blocks, the body's trailing newline and any front matter are kept as they are. A block that no longer parses as its kind after editing simply becomes what it now is (a paragraph that gained `# ` is a heading).

## How it is built (LES-6)
- **Parsing with positions**: the body is split into top-level blocks with their exact source ranges, by the markdown parser the app already renders with; the read view renders each block, the editor edits one block's range. A save splices the edited text into the body at that range: one function, tested on its own against the cases above.
- **Each block's look** comes from TAS-90's text style tokens, used by both the block's rendering and its `InlineEdit`, so reading and editing a block line up by construction.
- **The same component** can edit a doc in the Docs view later, block by block, instead of its whole source.

## Acceptance check
- Splice round-trip: for each case in the table, editing a block and saving it unchanged leaves the body byte for byte the same; an edit changes only its own range. (Core-level tests over a corpus of markdown, edge cases included.)
- In the app: double-clicking a paragraph, a heading and a code block edits each in place at its own style (its text's bounds the same reading and editing), the rest rendered; Esc drops, leaving saves; arrows walk into the next block; a task box toggles from reading.
- scripts/check passes.

Progress, plus one decision for you.
Built and tested so far:

- The ui/text module (the Docs view now uses the same renderer).

The decision: putting the caret exactly where you click inside rendered markdown. The renderer (gpui-base, from longbridge/gpui-kit) knows which source byte every rendered character came from, but it only exposes that for a selection, and it works the selection out while painting. A plain click leaves no selection, so it reports nothing. Toggling a task box from reading has the same problem: the renderer has no click hook for its checkboxes. The options:
A) (my recommendation) Patch gpui-base with two small public APIs, source_offset_at(point) and a task-box click callback, and send them upstream as a pull request. Until it's merged we build against the patched copy, either a fork referenced from Cargo.toml (needs a GitHub repo of yours to push to) or vendored into the repo (about 116k lines). Result: the caret is exact everywhere, and task boxes toggle from reading.
B) No patch. On a click, fake a drag from the click point to the line's end so the renderer computes a selection, then read where it starts. Exact, but for one frame the rest of the line flashes highlighted, and it depends on how the renderer behaves inside.
C) No patch. Open the editor and place the caret at the same point in the source text. Exact on plain text, but after **bold** or a link it lands a few characters off, because the source is wider than what you see.
Until you choose, the caret goes to the end of the block. Which do you want, and for A, a fork or a vendored copy?

---

## Plan (Claude)

Activity becomes one **timeline drawn on a rail**: a git graph's lanes, read like Linear's activity. The same component later draws the Activity view's feed and an agent's work.

### What it looks like
- **The rail.** A thin line runs down the left of the Activity section. Each event is a **mark on the rail**, and the rail connects every mark to the next. Nothing floats as a separate block.
- **Each kind of event has its own mark, all the same shape**: a 20px circle on the rail with a 12px glyph in it.
  - A state move wears the new state's mark, in that state's colour.
  - A note wears its author's avatar.
  - A link or unlink wears the link icon, a doc the doc icon.
  - A priority change wears the priority glyph; created wears the kind's icon.
  - A session or run wears Claude's icon: started, asks, allowed or denied, ended.
- **System events are one quiet line beside their mark**, as in Linear: "you moved it to Doing · 2h", "Claude linked TAS-90 · 5m".
  - Four or more in a row with nothing else between them fold into "6 more changes", which opens in place.
  - **Notes are cards** beside their avatar, as now, so a conversation still reads as one.
- **Lanes, as a git graph.** The human's events sit on the main rail.
  - A Claude session or run that works on the task **branches off** onto its own lane where its first event is, carries its events (notes, asks, link changes), and **merges back** at its last event or its end.
  - Two sessions at once show as two lanes side by side. A lane wears its run's colour and is named once, where it branches off ("Claude · build").
  - With a single actor, the timeline is just the rail.
- **Needs you** sits on the lane of the run that waits, at its last mark, with Allow / Deny as now.
- **Motion** (quiet, none when Reduce Motion is on):
  - a new event's mark grows in, and the rail draws down to it;
  - a branch eases out from the rail and back in;
  - folded changes open with the panel's slide.

### How it is built (LES-6)
- **The layout is model logic, not drawing**: `model::timeline` turns a node's events into rows. Each row has its lane, the lanes running past it, whether it branches or merges, and its fold group. It is pure, so it is tested on its own: one actor gives one lane; overlapping sessions get separate lanes; a lane merges at its last event; folding takes four or more system events in a row; a note is never folded.
- **One table of event kinds**, `ui/timeline/kinds.rs`. Each kind has its mark (glyph, colour), its line ("moved it to …") and whether it folds. The panel, the Activity view and the agents view all read from it, replacing `event_line`'s match. A new kind of event is a row there.
- **One `Timeline` component**, `ui/timeline/`, drawing rows on the rail. The rail, lanes and connectors are painted on a canvas from the rows, and the lines and cards are ordinary elements beside them. The task panel is its first user; the Activity view and agents view can switch to it after.
- `docs/design.md` gains a **Timeline** part (rail, marks, lanes, folding), so the grammar says it first.

### Acceptance check
- Model tests for the layout: lanes, branch and merge, overlapping sessions, folding rules, notes never folded, order newest first.
- App tests:
  - every event of a task shows as a mark on the rail, in order;
  - a run's events sit on its own lane;
  - four state changes in a row fold, and a click opens them;
  - a note's card still renders markdown;
  - Needs you sits at the run's last mark with Allow / Deny working.
- How it looks and moves is judged in the running app (build released for you to try).
- scripts/check passes.

data.body:
I want to attach links, images, or documents or files to the tasks.

documents could be saved as attachments alongside images and any other file.

but image could also be able to put in the body and markdown rendering to render them too, so copied image could be placeable in the markdown body or something.

---

## Goal
A task carries what its work needs: links, images, documents and any other file, attached from the CLI or the app. An image can also sit inline in the body: paste a copied image (or drop one) and it shows where it was put. Every attachment is in the task's history, in git with the log, and readable by a Claude run on that task.

## How it fits the vision
A task is the one unit a product's work moves through (plan → run → review → release). Attachments make it carry its own context: the screenshot of the bug, the spec PDF, the design link. Because `livtk show` lists each attachment's absolute path, a Claude run reads them as it reads the body: it can open images and PDFs itself. Files go through git like the log does, so a branch or worktree of the task has them too. Pipelines and releases will be able to use the same model later (build artifacts, release notes images).

## Decisions
- **One model.** An attachment is a file or a URL on a node: `{id, name, size, mime}` plus either a `blob` (sha256) or a `url`. Two new ops, `attach.add` / `attach.remove` (format v9), following the `doc.link` precedent: these are real things with history and an Activity mark, not a prop.
- **Content-addressed, committed.** File bytes go to `.livtk/attachments/<sha256>.<ext>`, written once, deduplicated, committed with `events.jsonl`. The log stays text and union-mergeable.
- **Size limit, configurable.** `[attachments] max_size` in `.livtk/config.toml`, default 25 MB. A bigger file is refused with a message saying to link it instead.
- **Inline images are attachments.** A pasted or dropped image becomes an attachment, and the body gets `![name](.livtk/attachments/<sha>.png)`, a project-relative path that humans, Claude and the app all resolve the same way.
- **Removing unlinks only.** The blob stays: older events and bodies still point at it. Cleaning up unreferenced blobs is a separate task if it is ever needed.

## Parts (each planned and acknowledged on its own)
1. Core and CLI: model, storage, ops, store, `livtk attach`, `show`, `export`.
2. App panel: the Attachments section, adding (picker, URL, drop), opening, the image viewer, the Activity mark.
3. Inline images in the body: rendering, paste and drop into the body editor.

## Acceptance check
- Parts 1 to 3 are done.

data.title: Attachments in the core and CLI: files and links on a task, stored by content, in its history
data.body:
## Goal
A task can have files and links attached with `livtk attach`. The files are stored once by content in `.livtk/attachments/` and committed. `livtk show` lists each attachment with its absolute path, so a Claude run can read it.

## Approach
- `livtk-core/src/attachments.rs` (new module, the one source of truth):
  - `Attachment { id, name, size, mime, source: Blob(sha256) | Url(String) }`.
  - `store_blob(path)`: sha256 the file (stream it, don't read it all into memory), copy it to `.livtk/attachments/<sha>.<ext>` if it isn't there already, and give the mime from the extension.
  - `blob_path(root, att)`: the file's path.
  - `max_size` comes from config.
- `event.rs`: add the `Op::AttachAdd { data }` and `Op::AttachRemove { id }` ops, at format v9. Update `name()`, `min_version()` and `subjects()`. An older livtk skips v9 lines, as it does for any newer format.
- `workspace.rs`: add `Command::Attach` / `Command::Detach`.
  - Validation: the file exists and fits `max_size`; a URL is http(s); a name can be given.
  - `attachments_of(node)` also reports when a blob is missing.
- `store.rs`:
  - New table `attachments(node, id, name, size, mime, blob, url, at, by)`.
  - Add apply arms and a query, add the table to the rebuild's reset list, and bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` (that triggers a rebuild, not a migration).
- `config.rs`: add an `[attachments] max_size` setting, default 25 MB. It is validated like the other project settings.
- `signal.rs`: add `attach.added` and `attach.removed`.
- Init's `.livtk/.gitignore` does not ignore `attachments/`, so the files are committed. `.gitattributes` marks `attachments/** binary`.
- `export.rs`: the export gets an attachments section.
- CLI (`main.rs`, `output.rs`):
  - `livtk attach add KEY <PATH|URL>... [--name N]`
  - `livtk attach list KEY`
  - `livtk attach remove KEY ID`
  - `show` (text and `--json`) lists attachments: id, name, size, and the absolute path or URL.
  - `describe` gets log lines for the two new ops.
- The app's exhaustive matches on `Op` (timeline `Mark`, `kinds.rs`, `activity.rs`) get the minimal arms needed to compile. They are given their real look in the app panel task.
- Plugin skills: `livtk:work` says that a task's attachments are part of its context, read through the paths in `livtk show`.

## Files
- `crates/livtk-core/src/{attachments.rs (new), lib.rs, event.rs, workspace.rs, store.rs, signal.rs, export.rs}` and the config module
- `crates/livtk-cli/src/{main.rs, output.rs}`
- `crates/livtk-core/tests/attachments.rs` (new), `crates/livtk-cli` tests
- `crates/livtk-app/src/model/{timeline.rs, activity.rs}`, `ui/timeline/kinds.rs` (compile-only arms)
- `plugin/skills/work`, `docs/plan.md` (data model and storage sections)

## Acceptance check
- `livtk attach add TAS-X ./shot.png https://example.com/spec`, then `livtk show TAS-X`. Expected: both are listed, the file with an absolute path under `.livtk/attachments/<sha>.png` that exists, and the link with its URL. The history shows two "attached" lines.
- The same file attached to two tasks is stored once (one blob).
- A file over `max_size` is refused with a message that names the limit and suggests a link. Nothing is written.
- `livtk attach remove TAS-X ID` takes it off `show`, and the blob is still on disk.
- Deleting `livtk.db` and running any command rebuilds the same attachments from the log.
- `cargo test -p livtk-core -p livtk-cli` passes, including new tests for these cases and for a v8 reader skipping v9 lines.

data.title: Attachments in the task panel: listed, added by picker, URL or drop, opened, images viewed
data.body:
## Goal
A task's panel shows its attachments. Files and links can be added and removed there, and a file can be dropped onto the panel. A click opens an attachment: an image in a viewer in the middle, a file in its default app, a link in the browser. Each attach or detach is a mark on the Activity rail.

## Approach
- **docs/design.md first.** Add a section to Parts about attachments:
  - Where they sit: an "Attachments" section label after Links, before the body, since it is metadata in the panel.
  - The row: a type icon (or a small thumbnail for an image), the name, the size or host quiet after it, and × to remove.
  - The empty state: no section at all, only the add button in the Links row's actions.
  - Image viewer: the image takes the list's place behind a header bar (name, Open, Reveal, close), and Esc gives the list back.
- **Model** (`model.rs` `Detail`, `load_detail`): `attachments: Vec<AttachmentRow>` from `Workspace::attachments_of`. Add `attach(paths)`, `attach_url(url)` and `detach(id)` beside `link_doc`.
- **Panel** (`ui/detail.rs`): the Attachments section, its rows built like `doc_group`.
  - Add button (paperclip icon, tooltip "Attach"). It opens a menu: "Files…" (`prompt_for_paths` with `files: true, multiple: true`) and "Link…" (one URL field, Enter adds it).
  - Drop: the panel accepts external file drops (GPUI `ExternalPaths`) and shows an `ACCENT` outline while files hover over it.
  - Refusals (too big, missing) show as the panel's usual error line, with the core's message.
- **Opening:** one helper, `open_external(target)`, in one place. A web link goes through the existing `cx.open_url`. A file uses gpui's `open_with_system` if this gpui has it, else `open` / `xdg-open`. "Reveal" shows the file in Finder.
- **Image viewer** (`ui/attachment_view.rs`, new): a full-middle surface showing the image fit to the box (`img(path)`).
- **Activity:** add the `Mark::Attach` / `Mark::Detach` rows to `ui/timeline/kinds.rs` (paperclip glyph; the line is "attached shot.png" or "removed shot.png"). The Activity feed line goes in `model/activity.rs`. Small changes fold as other marks do.
- Refreshing: an attach from the CLI shows in the open panel through the existing log watch, with nothing new to add.

## Files
- `docs/design.md`
- `crates/livtk-app/src/model.rs`, `model/timeline.rs`, `model/activity.rs`
- `crates/livtk-app/src/ui/detail.rs`, `ui/timeline/kinds.rs`, `ui/attachment_view.rs` (new), `ui/mod.rs` (open helper, viewer routing, Esc), `ui/icons.rs` (paperclip, file, image)
- `crates/livtk-app/tests/app/attachments.rs` (new, in the one app test binary)

## Acceptance check
- App tests (behaviour, not looks):
  - attaching a file through the model lists it in the detail;
  - a dropped path attaches it;

data.title: Inline images in a task's body: pasted or dropped where the caret is, rendered in place
data.body:
## Goal
An image copied to the clipboard and pasted into a body block, or an image file dropped onto the body, becomes an attachment. Its markdown image goes in where the caret (or the drop) is. The body renders it in place, and a click opens it in the viewer.

## Approach
- **Rendering.** One shared resolver for local images. Extract `local_images()` from `model/docs.rs` into a shared helper that takes a base dir; Docs and bodies both call it, with no copy. A body's images resolve against the project root, so `.livtk/attachments/<sha>.png` works. First check that gpui-component 0.7.3's `TextView` draws image nodes from a path. If it does not, add an image block to the shared renderer in `ui/text/markdown.rs`, as callouts and mermaid have, using `img(path)` fit to the column's width.
- **Blocks.** `md.rs` gets no new block kind: an image is markdown in a paragraph, so splice and block edits keep it as text. In read mode a block that is only an image shows the image. Double-clicking it edits its markdown, like any block.
- **Paste.** In the body's `InlineEdit`, Cmd-V first checks the clipboard for an image (`ClipboardEntry::Image`). If there is one, the image's bytes go through the core's `store_blob` (from bytes, named `pasted-<time>.png`), and `![pasted-…](.livtk/attachments/<sha>.png)` is inserted at the caret. Text paste is unchanged.
- **Drop.** An image file dropped onto a body block is attached and inserted after that block, as its own block. A non-image file dropped onto the body is attached and inserted as a link: `[name](.livtk/attachments/<sha>.pdf)`.
- **Click.** A body image opens in the attachment viewer from TAS-95. A link to an attachment opens it as the panel does, through the one open helper.
- The core gets `attach_bytes(node, name, bytes)` next to the file path API, so paste and the CLI share one way in.

## Files
- `crates/livtk-core/src/attachments.rs`, `workspace.rs` (bytes entry point)
- `crates/livtk-app/src/model/docs.rs` (extracted resolver), `model.rs`
- `crates/livtk-app/src/ui/text/{markdown.rs, blocks.rs, inline_edit.rs}`, `ui/detail.rs`
- `crates/livtk-app/tests/app/attachments.rs`, `crates/livtk-core/tests/attachments.rs`

## Acceptance check
- Tests:
  - pasting image bytes into a body block attaches one blob and puts its markdown at the caret, and the rest of the block is unchanged;
  - pasting text is unchanged;
  - dropping a PNG on a block inserts an image block after it;
  - dropping a PDF inserts a link;
  - a body image's path resolves to the absolute file;
  - the Docs reader's images still resolve (existing test).
- In the app: take a screenshot to the clipboard (Cmd-Ctrl-Shift-4), click into a task's body and press Cmd-V. The screenshot shows in the body where the caret was, and under Attachments. Clicking it opens the viewer. `livtk show` prints the markdown with a path Claude can read.

In the edit mode, the text loses it's height as it was in the reader moder, the edit line height is a bit less and maybe some font adjustment's are different too. So identify what's the problem there and give me plan what you would change

## Goal
A block being edited keeps the size, line height, spacing and colour it has when read: switching between reading and editing moves no line and changes no glyph's look.

## What is wrong (found by reading the code; not yet measured)
- A plain paragraph matches: both are 14px on a 22px line in the same font (our style beats the Textarea's own `rems(1.25)` and `.xsmall()` size), with no extra padding.
- **Lists are where editing gets shorter.** When read, gpui-base puts 3.5px between items (`node.rs:3388`, body × 0.25), and our task-list renderer puts 4px (`markdown.rs:97`, `gap_1`). In the editor the items are plain lines with no gap, so each line after the first moves up by about 4px.
- **Headings round differently.** `HEADING_LINES` are ratios, so some lines come out fractional: H3 is 15 × 1.35 = 20.25px. The reader snaps that to the device pixel (20.5), but the editor rounds to a whole pixel (20), so it is shorter. H5 goes the other way (17.5 when read, 18 when edited).
- **Colour, which looks like a font change.** The reader draws in the theme's foreground, `TEXT` #f7f8f8, but the editor uses the Body role's `TEXT_2` #d0d6e0, so the edited text looks dimmer and thinner. A code block's background is `SURFACE` when read and `HOVER` when edited.
- **Quotes.** When read, a quote has a muted colour, a bar and an indent. When edited it is plain `> ` text.
- **Why the tests pass anyway.** The editor box gets `min_h` equal to the read height (`inline_edit.rs:268`), so the "as tall" checks in `tests/app/ui.rs` compare outer boxes, not where the lines are.
- **Not traced yet.** A paragraph with inline code is laid out a different way (`inline_flow.rs`) and may come out taller than 22px.

## Approach
1. **Test first.** Add a test that measures real line positions in both modes: the first and last line's top in the TextView against the Textarea's line height and line count. Do this for a paragraph, a paragraph with inline code, a list, a task list, H1–H6 and a code block, and compare without the `min_h` pin. The test confirms the causes above and catches anything they miss.
2. **Line heights as whole pixels in the style table.** Store each heading's line in `style.rs` as a whole-pixel value rather than a ratio, and choose heading sizes whose line in the reader's fixed ratio also lands on a whole pixel. The table stays the one source of truth for both modes.
3. **Colour.** Give Body and Heading the colour the reader actually draws (`TEXT`). Give the code role the reader's `SURFACE` background, and fix the comment at `style.rs:142`.
4. **List spacing.** Edit list items with the reader's item gap, so the lines sit where they read: style the Textarea's paragraph spacing if gpui-base allows it, otherwise give each item line the gap through our own list editing. Make the task-list renderer use the same token, defined in `style.rs` (not `gap_1`). If neither is possible in gpui-base 0.7.3, I'll note that here and ask before doing anything wider.
5. Quotes stay plain source when edited: the marker is the markdown being edited. Only their colour and indent are brought in line with the reader where the style table can do it.

## Files
`crates/livtk-app/src/ui/text/style.rs`, `inline_edit.rs`, `markdown.rs` (task-list gap), `tests/app/ui.rs` (the measuring test).

## Acceptance check
- `cargo test -p livtk-app --test app` passes, including the new test: in every block kind above, each line's top is the same reading and editing, within 0.5px.
- In the app: click into a paragraph, a list, an H3 and a code block. The text does not move or change colour when edit mode opens, and it does not move when edit mode closes.

data.body:
## Goal
An image copied to the clipboard and pasted into a body block, or an image file dropped onto the body, becomes an attachment. Its markdown image goes in where the caret (or the drop) is. The body renders it in place, and a click opens it in the viewer.

## What the libraries give (checked in the registry sources)
- gpui-component's text input has `on_paste(|item, window, cx| -> bool)` (`input/input.rs:379-400`), made for this. The handler sees the `ClipboardItem`, and returning `true` stops the text paste. The body's `InlineEdit` is that input, so paste needs no key handling of our own.
- gpui-pre has `ClipboardEntry::Image(Image)` (`platform.rs:3014`) and `ExternalPaths` for drops (`interactive.rs:694`).
- The markdown renderer (gpui-base `text/format/markdown.rs:850`, `text/node.rs:674-707`) does parse `![](...)` into image nodes. **But** it gives every URL other than `data:` to GPUI as `Resource::Uri`, which is fetched over HTTP, and this app sets no HTTP client. So an image from a local path does not load: not in bodies, and probably not in the Docs reader either, whose `local_images()` only makes the path absolute. Only `data:` URLs are decoded inline.

## Approach
- **Rendering.** Our shared renderer (`ui/text/markdown.rs`) gets an image block parser, as callouts and mermaid have. A paragraph that is only a local image (an attachment path, or a path relative to the doc) is drawn with `img(PathBuf)`. That is `Resource::Path`, read from disk, fit to the column's width and kept at its own size when smaller. Web images stay as they are.
  - One resolver decides what a path means: extract `local_images()` from `model/docs.rs` into a shared helper that takes a base dir. The base dir is the doc's folder for a doc, and the project root for a body. Docs and bodies both use it, so this also fixes images in the Docs reader.
  - Not chosen: rewriting to `data:` URLs. That base64-encodes whole files into the text on every load.
- **Blocks.** `md.rs` gets no new block kind: an image is markdown in a paragraph, so splice and block edits keep it as text. In read mode, a block that is only an image shows the image, and double-clicking it edits its markdown like any block.
- **Paste.** The body's `InlineEdit` sets `on_paste`. If the item holds a `ClipboardEntry::Image`, its bytes go through the core's `attach_bytes` (named `pasted-<time>.<ext>`, the extension from the image's format), `![pasted-…](.livtk/attachments/<sha>.<ext>)` is inserted at the caret, and the handler returns `true`. A copied file (`ExternalPaths`) is attached the same way. Anything else returns `false`, so text paste is unchanged.
- **Drop.** An image file dropped onto a body block is attached and inserted after that block, as its own block. Any other file dropped on the body is attached and inserted as a link: `[name](.livtk/attachments/<sha>.pdf)`.
- **Click.** A body image opens in the attachment viewer from TAS-95. A link to an attachment opens it as the panel does, through the one open helper.
- **Core.** `attach_bytes(node, name, bytes)` sits next to the path API, so paste and the CLI share one way in.

## Files
- `crates/livtk-core/src/attachments.rs`, `workspace.rs` (bytes entry point)
- `crates/livtk-app/src/model/docs.rs` (resolver extracted to a shared place), `model.rs`
- `crates/livtk-app/src/ui/text/{markdown.rs, blocks.rs, inline_edit.rs}`, `ui/detail.rs`
- `crates/livtk-app/tests/app/attachments.rs`, `crates/livtk-core/tests/attachments.rs`

## Acceptance check
- Tests:
  - pasting a `ClipboardItem` with image bytes into a body block attaches one blob and puts its markdown at the caret, and the rest of the block is unchanged;
  - pasting text is unchanged;
  - dropping a PNG on a block inserts an image block after it, and dropping a PDF inserts a link;
  - a body image's path resolves to the absolute file, and the renderer gets an image block (not a URI) for it;
  - a doc's relative image resolves the same way (the existing Docs test still passes).
- In the app: take a screenshot to the clipboard (Cmd-Ctrl-Shift-4), click into a task's body and press Cmd-V. The screenshot shows in the body where the caret was, and under Attachments. Clicking it opens the viewer. A doc with a relative image shows the image. `livtk show` prints the markdown with a path Claude can read.

## Goal
A task's panel shows its attachments. Files and links can be added and removed there, and a file can be dropped onto the panel. A click opens an attachment: an image in a viewer in the middle, a file in its default app, a link in the browser. Each attach or detach is a mark on the Activity rail.

## What the libraries give (checked in the registry sources)
- gpui-pre has `cx.open_with_system(path)` (`app.rs:1918`), which opens a file in its default app, so no `open` / `xdg-open` of our own is needed. `cx.open_url` is already used for the web.
- gpui-pre has `ExternalPaths` (`interactive.rs:694`) for files dropped from Finder (`on_drop::<ExternalPaths>`, `drag_over::<ExternalPaths>`).
- gpui-component 0.7.3 ships an `Attachment` element (`attachment.rs`): a media thumbnail (`AttachmentMedia::src`), a title, a description, on_click, on_remove, a status and progress. Use it for the rows if it fits the grammar at our row sizes. Otherwise build the rows like `doc_group`, and note why it didn't fit.

## Approach
